newsitem.title: USA: Orange County Board okays $137 mln bond refunding.
newsitem.headline: Orange County Board okays $137 mln bond refunding.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., Board of Supervisors on Tuesday approved a proposed $137 million refunding of taxable pension obligation bonds, a county spokeswoman said.
Under the proposal, the county will issue about $136.6 million of debt to refund about $127 million of outstanding 1994 Series A pension bonds.
The county intends to come to market with the refunding bonds by January 15, officials said.
The county said it had received tender offers from nearly 67 percent of the bondholders.

County officials said the tender would complete the restructuring of the pension obligation bonds, provide much-needed budget relief to the county in the near-term, and result in a net present-value savings of about $2.0 million.
The county's Public Finance Advisory Committee approved the proposal last month, but the Board of Supervisors failed to act on the plan before the holiday break.
The Board of Supervisors voted 3-to-2 Tuesday to approve the refunding ahead of a January 15 deadline to pay off bondholders, county spokeswoman Diane Thomas said.
Critics of the refinancing proposal warned that it would expand the county's debt obligations and urged the county's supervisors to consider alternatives.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on December 6, 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June.
